observations: A rounded head shape fills the center, built from overlapping black scribble loops over warm ochre and teal washes, with two dark oval eye areas visible near the middle.
Bursts of yellow, blue, pink, and orange marks scatter across the upper region and right edge, sitting on top of the darker underlayer rather than blending into it.

A mouth area sits in the lower center, outlined in red and black with a row of small white shapes suggesting teeth; the dark opening between the tooth row and the surrounding strokes is narrow rather than gaping.
reading: Dense black loops pile over ochre and teal washes, building a rounded head that reads as both solid and restless. Two dark oval eye areas sit quietly in the middle ground while a red-edged mouth below bares a tight row of teeth without fully opening. Scattered yellow and pink marks across the upper field feel like static around a still center. The mood reads as alert, maybe uneasy.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, title neighbors #200 and #202 share a front-facing head format with visible teeth. Title order and recorded creation order align for this work and both neighbors.

connections.reason: Both use a front-facing rounded head with red-edged mouth and white tooth shapes, but #200 sits on a dark teal ground with stronger red line work, while #201 uses a grey ground with more ochre warmth.

#202 shares the front-facing head format with white teeth along the bottom edge, but its jaw drops into a large dark opening and its palette spreads into pink and teal against an olive ground rather than the grey of #201.

lookingQuestion: Where does your eye settle first — on the dark oval eye areas or the red-edged row of teeth — and what does that path through the image feel like?
ambiguities: The subject reads as an animal head but scribble density obscures whether specific features beyond eyes and mouth are present or implied.
The nifty-faces #94 comparison shows a heavily masked form with no clear mouth or eye parallel to this work and was excluded as a connection.
